about.s001: What we do & how we are organised
about.s002: What we do, and how we are organised
about.s003: ACTION integrates evidence-based reporting standards, intelligent research tools and capacity-building resources. Built by a multidisciplinary consortium of clinical epidemiologists, acupuncture clinicians, implementation scientists and health-informatics experts, it serves researchers, practitioners, methodologists and journal editors worldwide.
about.s006: We lead the development, validation and iterative update of acupuncture-specific reporting standards (CONSORT / STRICTA / SPIRIT / PRISMA / CARE / RIGHT / ARRIVE), aligned with EQUATOR principles.
about.s008: Study-type matching and report templates, automated completeness checking, and acupuncture-adapted implementation-science frameworks (CFIR / ERIC / RE-AIM).
about.s010: Guideline-interpretation tutorials, a case-analysis library and curated literature, plus methodological workshops and academic forums for early-career researchers.
about.s012: An open expert-consultation channel and user forum, plus an institutional collaboration network to share best practice and continuously improve our guidelines and tools.
about.s014: ACTION is governed by a two-tier organisational structure — an International Advisory Board and a Core Execution Team — to safeguard the methodological rigour, academic authority and practical applicability of the platform, and to steer the long-term development of acupuncture clinical research reporting standards.
about.s038: Why ACTION exists, and where it is heading
about.s040: Empowering high-quality, transparent acupuncture research worldwide
about.s041: To empower acupuncture researchers and clinicians worldwide to design, conduct and report high-quality, transparent, reproducible and translatable clinical research, by providing standardised guidelines, practical intelligent tools and accessible methodological training. We are committed to elevating the methodological quality of acupuncture clinical evidence and advancing the evidence-based development of acupuncture medicine.
about.s043: The world’s leading platform for acupuncture research methodology
about.s044: To become the world’s leading authoritative platform for acupuncture clinical research methodology and reporting standards; to drive the standardisation, internationalisation and real-world translation of acupuncture research; and to contribute robust, high-quality evidence for global traditional medicine and public-health practice.
about.s047: ACTION is academically led and non-profit. There are several ways researchers, institutions and journals can help raise the quality of acupuncture research.
about.s049: Reference ACTION-endorsed reporting guidelines in study design, manuscript preparation and peer review. Widespread adoption is the most direct way to raise research quality.
about.s051: Join our working groups for guideline revision, validation studies and pilot testing of new tools. Front-line experience makes guidelines fit for real-world research.
about.s053: Submit feedback on usability, guideline applicability and unmet needs, and contribute high-quality acupuncture cases to the case library.
about.s055: Universities, hospitals, institutes and societies can form formal partnerships, promote the platform internally and co-host academic activities.
about.s057: We welcome collaborative research, funding and resource sharing to advance new reporting standards, intelligent tools and implementation-science research.
about.s060: Get in touch with the ACTION team
about.s062: For guideline queries, tool access, expert consultation, collaboration and media. We aim to reply within 3–5 working days.
about.s066: The Affiliated Traditional Chinese Medicine Hospital, Guangzhou Medical University (Guangzhou Hospital of Acupuncture)
about.s068: No. 95, Tiankun Third Road, Tianhe District, Guangzhou
about.s073: Academic statement, data sources, disclaimer & terms
about.s075: ACTION is an academically led, non-profit platform. Its reporting guidelines are developed and validated under the methodology of the EQUATOR Network, through structured international expert consensus (including modified Delphi processes).
about.s076: The platform’s intelligent tools (reporting assistant, SRD, and CFIR / ERIC / RE-AIM) are currently in beta / demonstration. Their outputs are assistive references and do not replace the professional judgement of researchers, statisticians or peer review.
about.s078: Guideline items derive from the published international reporting standards and their acupuncture extensions (CONSORT / STRICTA / SPIRIT / PRISMA / CARE / RIGHT / ARRIVE).
about.s079: Sample data and citations shown in the tools come from published literature and are illustrative, intended to demonstrate functionality.
about.s080: Institution names, logos and external links belong to their respective owners and are provided for reference; they do not imply endorsement of this platform.
about.s082: Platform content is for academic and educational reference. It does not constitute clinical advice and does not replace the judgement of a licensed physician.
about.s083: AI-assisted features may produce inaccurate or incomplete output. Users must verify results before use; ACTION accepts no liability for consequences arising from use of the content.
about.s084: Third-party content reached through external links is the responsibility of its respective owners.
about.s086: Data handling: most tools currently run and store data locally in your browser (e.g. assessment history); expert-consultation requests are sent by email and used only to reply to your enquiry.
about.s087: Cookies & analytics: any usage analytics are used solely to improve the platform and not for personal identification.
about.s088: Intellectual property: copyright of ACTION-developed acupuncture extensions and platform content belongs to ACTION and the respective authors; please cite the source for non-commercial academic use.
about.s089: Terms of use: do not use the platform for unlawful purposes or misleading promotion. Content may be updated without prior notice.
about.s090: Last updated: July 2026. For questions about these statements, contact action_acu{'@'}163.com.

assistant.s014: Answer two or three quick questions. The tool determines your study type, auto-mounts the right reporting guidelines and recommends the appropriate statistical methods.
assistant.s016: Q1 · What kind of study is it?
assistant.s030: The full checklist of the guideline matched in step 1 is expanded automatically. Where a guideline spans several tables (an RCT covers the CONSORT main table, the abstract table and STRICTA), they are merged into one sequence. These are the very items journals ask you to submit alongside the manuscript; answer them one by one and the draft report is composed in one click.
assistant.s048: Data linkage (planned). Importing an existing baseline table or raw Excel data to auto-fill the results section is on the roadmap.
assistant.s060: Hand the manuscript over for an item-by-item check: every line is numbered, then each checklist item from step 2 is judged reported / vague / not reported — with line numbers and the quoted evidence where it is reported, and what to add where it is not. That is the table journals ask you to submit, filled in. The whole manuscript is then read once more to cross-check acupuncture logic and terminology.
assistant.rvHint: Paste the body of your manuscript here (references are not needed). Every line is numbered, then checked item by item against the checklist expanded in step 2, filling in “reported on line N” or the reason it is missing. The manuscript and its results are saved under your account so you can reopen them from “Check history” below; deleting a record also erases the manuscript.
assistant.rvTarget: Will be checked against the {n} items of {code}
assistant.rvNoItems: No checklist items have been entered for {code} yet, so it cannot be checked. Try another study type in step 1.
assistant.rvNeedLogin: The item-by-item check calls a large language model, so it needs a guest account. Everything else on the site stays open.
assistant.rvTruncated: The manuscript exceeds the per-run limit; only the first 300,000 characters were checked.
assistant.rvFailed: The check failed. Please try again later. {msg}
assistant.rvSrcShow: Show the manuscript that was checked
assistant.rvSrcJump: Locate these lines in the manuscript
assistant.rvHistDesc: Every submission leaves a record here, so you can reopen a result after closing or refreshing the page — failed runs included. Deleting a record also erases the stored manuscript.
assistant.rvHistEmpty: No checks yet. Once you run one, the result stays here for you to reopen.
assistant.rvHistConfirmDelete: Deleting this record also erases the manuscript and the quoted excerpts stored with it. This cannot be undone. Delete it?
assistant.ckDesc: Beyond the item-by-item check, the whole manuscript is read once more to cross-check four things: whether the intervention and the control arm have been mixed up, whether needling frequency and follow-up time points contradict each other, whether the sample-size calculation matches the number actually enrolled, and whether acupoint names follow the standard convention. This layer points at problems rather than fixing them — please verify each finding yourself.

ckRule.arm: Intervention and control arm confused with each other
ckRule.schedule: Needling frequency contradicts follow-up time points

ckEmpty.ok: Nothing of this kind was found on a full read of the manuscript.
ckEmpty.na: This check does not apply to the study design of this manuscript.
ckEmpty.unchecked: This check did not finish (the model call failed). It means neither that there is a problem nor that there is none — please verify manually.

assistant.ckCapped: Many findings of this kind; only the first {n} are listed.
assistant.ckTruncated: The manuscript exceeds the reading budget for whole-manuscript checks. Only the first part was read; the remainder was not cross-checked.
assistant.auditCross: Whole-manuscript cross-check complete: {issue} inconsistent · {warn} to verify · {ok} with no issue
assistant.s087: Draft, polish and translate report prose. **Usable on its own** — just give a few keywords or paste a passage; no draft and no prior check required. If you did fill in a draft in step 2 and ran step 3, the items judged “vague” or “not reported” are also listed below, and your edits can be written straight back to them.
assistant.s104: Export this draft as a file you can use straight away. It exports the stored draft itself — no need to generate a preview first.
assistant.s115: Exported PDF · added blinding & AE sections
assistant.s119: Interface preview · the tool is in closed beta. Apply for access to try the live version.
assistant._title: Reporting assistant {'|'} ACTION · End-to-end support for acupuncture research reporting
assistant._desc: The ACTION reporting assistant: a five-step guided workflow — study-type matching, online reporting templates, completeness checking, AI-assisted drafting suggestions, and export and sharing — covering the whole acupuncture clinical research reporting process.
assistant.shamNoteY: Sham / placebo-needle control: report STRICTA domain 6 (the control intervention) in full — sham point selection, depth, and whether current is delivered.
assistant.shamNoteN: No sham control: state the comparator used (waiting list / usual care / active control) and discuss the limitations of leaving participants unblinded.
assistant.tplCount: {n} items from {m} checklist table(s), merged into a single sequence
assistant.dfImportFailed: Item matching failed. Your draft and the original manuscript are saved — fill items in yourself, or run the check again in step 3.
assistant.dfImportDone: Imported “{name}”: {lines} lines, {filled} items filled in automatically, {blank} still empty — the empty ones are what the manuscript does not cover. Exports still use your original manuscript as the body text.
assistant.dfDeleteConfirm: Delete this draft? Everything you have written in it will be deleted too, and cannot be recovered.
assistant.dfTooLong: Item {no} exceeds {max} characters. Please shorten it before saving.
assistant.dfTooShort: The draft is under {min} characters, so step 3 cannot check it. Please fill in a few more items.
assistant.dfNeedLogin: Sign in to fill in and save your draft report item by item — it belongs to your account only. The checklist itself is visible without signing in.
assistant.dfTitlePh: e.g. Electroacupuncture for knee osteoarthritis: an RCT
assistant.dfItemPh: Write the content this item asks for…
assistant.dfPreviewEmpty: Answer the items on the left, then select “Generate draft report”. Your text is composed into continuous prose section by section, with a “to be completed” marker for any required item left blank — ready for step 3.
assistant.dfMissing: {n} required item(s) still empty — marked “to be completed” in the draft
assistant.tplEmpty: No checklist items have been entered for this guideline yet.
assistant.auditDesc: Everything this run did is recorded here — what was submitted, which models judged it, and how it came out — so the conclusion can be traced back.
assistant.auditSubmitted: Submitted a manuscript ({chars} characters) to be checked against {code}
assistant.auditJudged: {n} items judged: {ok} reported · {vague} vague · {miss} not reported — {pct}% complete
assistant.diffV3_1: Added a paragraph on blinding of outcome assessors
assistant.diffV3_2: Added three mild adverse events (subcutaneous bruising)
assistant.diffV3_3: Removed follow-up time points duplicated from the methods
assistant.diffV2_1: Revised the sample-size basis (120 → 96, with reasons for attrition)
assistant.diffV2_2: Added a STRICTA-compliant description of de qi

stageDesc.draft: Start from the structured template in step 2, answer the checklist item by item, then generate a draft.
stageDesc.manuscript: The item-by-item template in step 2 will not help. Go straight to step 3 and have the manuscript checked.

assistant.stageGoDraft: Go to step 2 · fill in the template
assistant.stageGoReview: Go to step 3 · check the manuscript
assistant.skipHint: You chose “I already have a manuscript”. The item-by-item template here is for writing from scratch — stay if you want to see what the checklist looks like, or go straight to step 3 to have your manuscript checked.
assistant.rvFromDraft: This manuscript came from the draft generated in step 2. You already answered the checklist item by item, so completeness will mostly come back full — what is worth reading here are the items judged vague, and the logic and terminology cross-check below.
assistant.wkNeedLogin: This step edits your own draft report, so please sign in first.
assistant.wkNeedDraft: You have no draft yet. Everything above works regardless; fill in a few checklist items in step 2 and a list of “what still needs work” will appear here as well.
assistant.wkNeedReview: This draft has not been checked yet. Everything above works regardless; once step 3 finishes, the items needing work are also listed here and can be written straight back.
assistant.wkLead: Step 3 flagged {n} item(s). After revising, run step 3 again to see how many vague items are left.
assistant.wkAllClear: Every item in this draft is judged as reported. Nothing left to revise.
assistant.wkNoText: This item has no text yet — use “Draft” to start from keywords.
assistant.wkKwPh: e.g. electroacupuncture, dense-disperse, 2/100 Hz, 30 min retention
assistant.wkNeedTextTip: Polishing and translation rewrite existing text; this item has none yet

wkSoloLead.continue: Give a few keywords and get the passage this section calls for. Paste any half-written text below and it will be continued.
wkSoloLead.polish: Paste the passage to polish below and pick a style. Every data point and qualifier is kept — only the wording changes.
wkSoloLead.translate: Paste the Chinese passage below to get publication-ready academic English, using the terminology conventional in international acupuncture research.

assistant.wkSoloKwPh: e.g. electroacupuncture, dense-disperse wave, 2/100 Hz, 30 min retention
assistant.wkSoloTextPh: Paste the passage to work on…
assistant.wkSoloTextOptPh: (optional) Paste any half-written text here and it will be continued…
assistant.wkCopyFailed: Copy failed — please select the text above manually.
assistant.wkSavePickItem: Choose an item to write into…
assistant.wkNote: The model never fabricates study data: sample sizes, p values, follow-up durations and anything else not supplied are left as “[to be completed]” placeholders rather than guessed. Always verify a suggestion before applying it.

expDesc.docx: The manuscript itself, split by section, with the reporting checklist appended
expDesc.xlsx: The checklist journals ask you to submit alongside the manuscript, with check results
expDesc.json: Structured record for importing into your own workflow or batch analysis

assistant.expNote: Unanswered required items are marked “[To be completed: item x]” in the manuscript so you can find them; conditional items leave no trace. No PDF — server-side Chinese PDF generation depends on fonts installed on the server, and a missing font renders as tofu blocks rather than an error. Save to PDF from Word instead.
assistant.auditApplied: Applied an AI rewrite to item {no} ({chars} characters)

guidelines.s002: Find the guideline for your study design
guidelines.s003: Every acupuncture clinical study maps to one reporting-guideline set. Filter by study type, then open a set to preview its checklist, download the Chinese / English documents and read the source article.
guidelines.s012: Extends CONSORT for reporting acupuncture interventions in RCTs: points, needling, de qi.
guidelines.s017: Extends SPIRIT (TCM Extension 2018) with standard protocol items for acupuncture trials.
guidelines.s022: Extends PRISMA with reporting items for acupuncture systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
guidelines.s026: Extends CARE: the acupuncture case-report guideline hosted and developed by ACTION.
guidelines.s031: Extends RIGHT with reporting items for acupuncture clinical practice guidelines.
guidelines.s035: ARRIVE 2.0 for reporting in vivo animal research behind acupuncture mechanism studies.
guidelines.s040: Read the checklist, download in your language
guidelines.s041: Open a set to read its scope and checklist, download the Chinese or English document, or open the source article for the full explanation and elaboration. Documents are provided on equal footing in both languages.
guidelines.s044: STRICTA (Standards for Reporting Interventions in Clinical Trials of Acupuncture) is a CONSORT extension. It specifies how acupuncture interventions should be reported in RCTs: acupuncture rationale, needling details (points, depth, response sought), treatment regimen, co-interventions, practitioner background and control/comparator.
guidelines.s045: 17 items across 6 domains, cross-referenced with the CONSORT and (for protocols) SPIRIT statements.
guidelines.s054: The SPIRIT-TCM Extension 2018 adapts the SPIRIT statement (Standard Protocol Items: Recommendations for Interventional Trials) for traditional Chinese medicine, including acupuncture. It guides what a trial protocol must pre-specify, so the planned methods are transparent before the trial begins.
guidelines.s055: Use at the design stage; pairs with STRICTA / CONSORT when the trial is reported.
guidelines.s065: PRISMA for Acupuncture provides reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses that synthesise acupuncture evidence, addressing how acupuncture-specific characteristics (intervention details, syndrome differentiation, sham/placebo controls) should be handled in evidence synthesis.
guidelines.s066: Built on the PRISMA statement; use when reporting evidence syntheses of acupuncture trials.
guidelines.s074: Case report / series · extends CARE · hosted by ACTION
guidelines.s076: CARE for Acupuncture extends the CARE (CAse REport) statement to acupuncture case reports and case series. Developed under the EQUATOR methodology by an international, multidisciplinary panel, it adds the acupuncture-specific detail that generic case-report guidance omits — needle type, point selection and operation, syndrome differentiation, de qi, and adverse events.
guidelines.s077: Final checklist: 13 domains, 30 items. Source published in BMJ Evidence-Based Medicine (2025).
guidelines.s096: Try it in the reporting assistant to auto-check completeness item by item.
guidelines.s100: RIGHT for Acupuncture extends the RIGHT (Reporting Items for practice Guidelines in HealThcare) statement to clinical practice guidelines that include acupuncture recommendations, so guideline developers report the evidence base, recommendation strength and acupuncture specifics transparently.
guidelines.s101: Use when developing or reporting acupuncture-related clinical practice guidelines.
guidelines.s107: Animal experiment · in vivo research reporting
guidelines.s109: ARRIVE 2.0 (Animal Research: Reporting of In Vivo Experiments) governs the reporting of animal studies — the mechanism and pre-clinical research that underpins acupuncture science. The 'Essential 10' plus the recommended set cover study design, sample size, randomisation, blinding, outcome measures and statistics.
guidelines.s110: An international standard adopted as-is; use for acupuncture mechanism / pre-clinical studies.
guidelines.s118: Reporting guidelines are living documents. ACTION records each set's current version, registration and publication status, and its update commitment — so you always cite the version you actually used.
guidelines.s128: EQUATOR-registered 26 Oct 2018; protocol 2019; guideline in BMJ Evid-Based Med, 24 Jun 2025. Update planned within 5 years.
guidelines.s133: Revised STRICTA, extending the CONSORT statement.

guidelines.s154: On versioning. ACTION hosts and iterates the acupuncture extensions (CARE for Acupuncture and others) under the EQUATOR network's methodology; extensions of external statements (CONSORT, SPIRIT, PRISMA, RIGHT, ARRIVE) track their upstream versions. Always cite the exact version used in your study.
guidelines.s156: How CARE for Acupuncture was tested
guidelines.s157: Before release, the CARE for Acupuncture checklist was pilot-tested through a structured, international expert-consensus process — so the final items reflect tested agreement, not a single group's opinion.
guidelines.s158: An international, multidisciplinary panel — clinicians, researchers, methodologists and journal editors — refined an initial 31-item checklist through three rounds of modified Delphi surveys, following the EQUATOR network's recommended method. Items reaching ≥80% consensus were retained; those between 50–80% were revised; below 50% were excluded. One item (diagnostic challenges) was dropped, yielding a final checklist of 13 domains and 30 items.
guidelines.s159: A sensitivity analysis and consistency evaluation gave a Kendall's coefficient of concordance of 0.163 (p<0.001) and a coefficient of variation of 15.1%, indicating good stability and internal consistency.
guidelines.s172: Source. Duan Y, Xu Z, Zhang Y, et al. CARE extension guideline for acupuncture case reports. BMJ Evidence-Based Medicine, 2025. doi:10.1136/bmjebm-2025-113641. Figures above are drawn from the published consensus study.

implementation.s003: Built on an acupuncture-adapted CFIR (Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research) with five domains. Two ways to work: match barriers to pre-curated strategies directly, or let AI distil barriers from your description and pull candidate strategies from the library. Either way you get a barrier–strategy optimisation report.
implementation.s006: Tick the constructs that are barriers in your setting. Each maps to pre-curated implementation strategies in the reference library, producing a barrier–strategy report directly.
implementation.s011: Describe your acupuncture implementation setting and the difficulties you face. The AI distils the underlying CFIR barriers, then pulls candidate strategies from the library for you to choose from.

srd.s017: How the assessment works · scale & decision rule
srd.s029: The four domains split into two key domains (Study topic and Study results KEY) plus two non-key domains: Study methods and Study quality.
srd.s030: The overall verdict is looked up from a matrix: the combined state of the two key domains sets the row, and the state of the non-key domains sets the column. Higher key-domain overlap dominates the result.
srd.s031: Example: if both key domains are “moderate/high”, the overall verdict is High regardless of the non-key domains.

srd._title: Methodology assessment {'|'} ACTION · Systematic Review Duplication (SRD)
srd._desc: ACTION Systematic Review Duplication (SRD) tool: import two systematic reviews and let AI assess overlap item by item against the SRD checklist (4 domains, ~40 items) and its overall-verdict matrix, producing an exportable table with verdicts, rationale and source quotations.

srd.scoreTitle: Item score (0–3; higher means more duplication)
srd.rt3Desc: Meets the item's 3-point anchor; no observable difference
srd.rt2Desc: Substantively aligned; the difference does not change the clinical or methodological reading
srd.rt1Desc: A material difference that changes the reading, but a clear common core remains
srd.rt0Desc: Meets the item's 0-point anchor; no substantive common ground
srd.rtUnclearDesc: Neither review reports it clearly, so no judgement is possible — excluded from both numerator and denominator
srd.scoreFormula: Higher scores mean more duplication. Domain maximum = 3 × number of items (Domain 1 /24, Domain 2 /18, Domain 3 /42, Domain 4 /18; /102 in total). Duplication % = score ÷ maximum × 100, then binned by the scale below. Items with insufficient evidence are dropped from the denominator together with their 3 points — two reviews both being vague is not the same as two reviews doing the same thing.
srd.scoreDropped: Nominal maximum is {full}. In this run {n} item(s) had insufficient evidence and were dropped from the denominator along with their points.
